evals.prompt: Complete the host-side adapter for our first single-GPU cuDF query-engine proof of concept in /workspace/input/async-copy-cleanup. Read TASK.md and the supplied caller and interfaces, preserve the CPU reference and protected engine behavior, and repair only the allowed implementation. From the task directory run python run_checks.py to compile and execute the supplied tests. Return the patch, exact build/run commands, observed results and any remaining native checks. This environment executes a deterministic CPU simulation of asynchronous backend operations. Its checks establish the host contract only; CUDA/libcudf execution must be reported separately.
evals.expected_output: Repairs the allowed C++ implementation, builds it and runs python run_checks.py. The synchronous adapter preserves the required upload, output allocation, aggregation and wrapper-construction order. Exact sum/count matches the supplied CPU reference for nullable, empty and all-null inputs. Required owners survive queued consumers on normal completion, failure before submission, output allocation failure after upload submission, and result-wrapper failure. Each exercised std::bad_alloc propagates as the original error, queued work is completed before dependent owners are released, and a subsequent valid call succeeds. Reports actual commands and all supplied test outcomes without claiming the CPU simulation proves native cuDF execution.
assertions: Produces a concrete repair only to adapter.hpp, preserving public signatures, protected caller/checker and the required submission order.
Runs python run_checks.py, compiling the repaired C++20 program and reporting its actual full test outcome.
Returns exact sum/count for nullable, empty and all-null inputs.
Keeps every required buffer, resource and stream owner valid until queued consumers finish on success and the exercised allocation failures.
Preserves std::bad_alloc and verifies recovery with a subsequent valid call.
Distinguishes host-contract simulation results from unperformed native CUDA/libcudf validation.

evals.prompt: Complete the host-side adapter for our first cuDF execution path in /workspace/input/worker-result-handoff. Our engine sends a batch between workers, then consumes the returned result. Read TASK.md and the supplied interface, fix the allowed implementation, and run python run_checks.py from the task directory to compile and execute the supplied checks while preserving the existing caller and CPU reference. Return the patch, exact commands, observed comparison and remaining work. The supplied backend is a deterministic CPU simulation of queued GPU work, so a successful simulator run is not evidence that native cuDF ran.
evals.expected_output: Repairs adapter.hpp, builds it and runs python run_checks.py. submit returns with work still queued, honoring the caller's asynchronous contract. The returned QueryResult owns the input, staged/output buffers, producer and consumer streams, and allocation resource for their needed lifetimes. Consumer work waits for the correct producer dependency. get returns completed backend sum/count and can be called repeatedly; destruction before get also completes dependent work safely. Two outstanding results can be consumed independently in either order. Explicit CPU fallback remains allowed only when selected and is labeled Origin::cpu; a backend-selected request returns the backend operation's result. All supplied checks pass with clean ownership/queued-work audits. Reports actual simulator results separately from native cuDF checks still required.
assertions: Repairs only adapter.hpp and runs python run_checks.py with an observed full test result.
Preserves asynchronous submit, returning before queued work executes.
Retains required buffers, streams and resource owners after caller references expire, and establishes producer-to-consumer readiness.
Returns exact backend sum/count for normal, empty and all-null inputs; repeated get and independent outstanding results remain correct.
Safely completes dependent work when a result is destroyed before get.
Preserves explicit CPU fallback and labels its origin truthfully, without treating simulator Origin::backend as native cuDF evidence.

evals.expected_output: Corrects both ordinary result destruction order and exceptional pending-work lifetime. Declares/retains context so table and descriptor are destroyed before context, and keeps required input owners plus context outside the throwing scope until finish covers all submitted work. Catches exceptions around native submission and descriptor construction, calls finish before local owners/table can unwind, then rethrows the original exception. A correct synchronous strategy may finish immediately after submit before descriptor construction, but must also catch submit itself throwing after work was queued. The owning result is preserved rather than returning a view. The test protocol compares exact ordered CPU values across empty/cross-batch/bounds cases, drops the caller context, injects recoverable post-submission host allocation failure with pending-work observation, checks release order, and retries in the same context. Does not report a native POC pass or executed tests because only source-review inputs were supplied.
assertions: Shows corrected C++ that ensures table/descriptor destruction precedes their required context owners.
Retains inputs and context across native calls that can throw after submitting work.
Completes pending work before releasing dependent objects on both success and exception paths, preserving the original exception.
Does not propose only a successful-return wait or a guard destroyed after the owning objects it must protect.
Keeps an owning native result and preserves the full OFFSET/LIMIT operation.
Defines exact comparison and failure-injection checks and marks build/native execution unperformed.

evals.expected_output: Keeps the existing engine scan and passes its host bytes to cuDF, without treating ScanToken as a path or introducing a new reader/credential/cache/retry subsystem. Retains the ScanLease owner, input GpuTable and query result in an outer scope; a try/catch covers every operation after submission and calls finish before those owners unwind, then rethrows. Establishes completion before returning the HostAnswer. Records that source bytes are pageable, retains ownership through the read, and does not describe them as pinned or require a production pinned-memory redesign. Names unavailable input/reference/build/runtime as prerequisites to running the native POC; provides build/run/CPU comparison and native-result-observation steps without fabricated results.
assertions: Provides a concrete corrected function retaining the ScanLease owner through all queued uses of its bytes.
Retains intermediate native owners until dependent consumers complete on exception as well as success.
Uses the existing engine host-buffer path and does not interpret ScanToken as an accessible object/file path.
Correctly identifies the supplied source bytes as pageable.
Preserves the complete selected query without adding production caching, retry, credential or distributed work.
Reports missing execution inputs as blockers and separates the proposed patch from unperformed runtime validation.

evals.expected_output: Identifies the exact conflict: selected query units<12 produces sum30000,count1 on the fixture, while CPU units<=12 and saved reference produce sum60000,count2. Asks the engineer which behavior is authoritative before committing one GPU predicate or changing the reference. Keeps useful pending work bounded: version/public API mapping and a boundary table can be prepared, but semantic selection is blocked. States both alternatives in the test table; covers units11/12/13, date lower included and upper excluded, rebate250/450 included and249/451 excluded, exact INT64 arithmetic under supported bounds. Does not turn absence of a GPU speedup into failure or assume the saved reference overrides the query.
assertions: Computes both conflicting results correctly and names the exact < versus <= mismatch.
Asks which behavior controls before selecting the GPU predicate or modifying CPU/reference behavior.
Does not silently repair one supplied source or assert overall POC completion.
Provides concrete tests for the supplied fixture and numeric/date boundaries with stated expected outcomes or clearly labeled unresolved alternatives.
Preserves the requested full native query as the implementation target once semantics are resolved.

evals.expected_output: Rejects the observed original run as native POC acceptance despite exact numerical agreement and a CUDA marker. Writes a replacement that uploads original rows, invokes cudf_selected_query and downloads that actual DeviceAnswer; CPU answer computation is removed from the GPU function while CPU path remains unchanged. Holds native owners outside the throwing scope and synchronizes on success and catch before releasing owners, then propagates the original error. Requires rebuild/rerun, exact comparison under the named CPU policy and the protected result-producing counter tied to the queried output. Nsight unavailability is recorded but is not a first-POC blocker when reliable engine evidence is available. Reports corrected code unexecuted and no overall native pass yet; absence of measured speedup alone is not failure.
assertions: Explains why matching CPU values plus an unrelated CUDA marker do not prove native result-producing execution.
Provides a concrete adapter replacement whose returned value depends on cudf_selected_query.
Preserves owners across all potentially throwing queued operations and completes consumers before cleanup.
Requires rebuilt/reexecuted output comparison and reliable result-producing cuDF evidence before POC acceptance.
Treats profiler absence as optional for this initial POC while keeping native execution evidence mandatory.
Does not claim the revised implementation was built, executed or passed.

evals.prompt: Build my query engine its first native cuDF GPU execution path and show that its output matches the CPU implementation. I have not supplied the repository, query, schema or CPU reference yet.
evals.expected_output: Asks for the target-engine code/build entry point, selected query or CPU implementation, input schema/fixture and expected result. Does not invent an engine or claim code was built or executed. Identifies the missing prerequisites as blocking implementation.
assertions: Identifies the missing target-engine inputs.
Asks focused questions needed to establish the actual POC.
Does not fabricate build, GPU execution or correctness results.

evals.prompt: I only need a pandas expression for a small CPU-only DataFrame named sales with columns region and revenue. Return total revenue by region, preserving missing region keys. No GPU or query-engine integration is involved.
evals.expected_output: Provides a pandas groupby expression equivalent to sales.groupby("region", dropna=False)["revenue"].sum(), without activating the query-engine builder or proposing a native GPU integration.
assertions: Does not load the query-engine builder skill.
Uses dropna=False to retain missing region keys.
Does not introduce GPU setup or engine integration work.
